intended_object: The probability density of the standard Student's t-distribution with ν > 0 degrees of freedom: f(x) = Γ((ν+1)/2) / (√(νπ) Γ(ν/2)) · (1 + x²/ν)^{-(ν+1)/2}. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body matches the textbook density exactly. The normalizing constant is Γ((ν+1)/2)/(√(νπ)·Γ(ν/2)), and it multiplies (1 + x²/ν)^(-(ν+1)/2). The base 1 + x²/ν is positive when ν > 0, so the real power `rpow` takes its usual value. The formula also applies to any real ν > 0, not only to integers, which is the usual generalization. When ν ≤ 0 the definition returns 0. The docstring says so explicitly, and it is the usual junk-value convention, since there is no law in that case. The density is a function of a real variable, so ℝ is its natural setting. I searched Mathlib for "student" and found no Student's t-distribution there (the only match was an unrelated file), so there is no more general Mathlib counterpart.
